In particular at least four distinct support-2 pairs are necessary; the disjoint two-pair/matching case is excluded.
written_argument: Each heavy row/column has mixed degree four: it contains two heavy full-D rays and two orthogonal support-2 rays. The two support-2 pairs must be disjoint and partition D, for equal pairs would fill their plane and force both heavy rays to avoid it. Suppose an axis a appears in just one support-2 pair U={a,b}. Every heavy line has exactly one U boundary cell and its other support-2 ray is on V=D\U. For each of the four full-D heavy core rays, its U projection is nonzero and perpendicular to its heavy-row and heavy-column U-boundary Q rays; these two rays are therefore collinear. Since the core is complete, all four U-boundary rays have the same ray x. The four V-boundary rays similarly have one common ray y. In the support-2 cell graph paired along low-only lines, the U cells decompose into two paths joining these four endpoints plus cycles. Both paths have x endpoints, hence odd length and one high-row plus one high-column endpoint. Grouping cycles by their projective 2D basis, the main x/x-perpendicular group has one x-ray per incident row and two fewer x-perpendicular rays than incident rows. Its two paths occupy at least four rows. A different U-basis cycle group is Q-nonorthogonal to it and, by the actual three-mate transition-support argument and light-e_a dimension saturation, would require at least five further rows, contradicting at most seven mixed rows. Thus for any mate its main-group span W has the main row count, its x-perpendicular class spans a codimension-two subspace, and the light-e_a rays span W-perpendicular. Every full-D heavy Q ray is perpendicular to x and has a nonzero U projection, hence overlaps x-perpendicular. All four corresponding mate rays therefore lie in the two-dimensional residual in W. Every heavy Q ray is perpendicular to both x and y and hence lies in the 2-space spanned by the complements of x and y in U and V. The actual 2x2 heavy row/column ONBs force its opposite Q rays collinear, so the four heavy mate rays are pairwise orthogonal: a contradiction in dimension two.
